body: **2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — set the origin of `contract/accessibility-tree/author-id` (every element node of a Dioxus document carries its stable id as AccessKit `author_id`, no TextRun / document-root / Window node does), the name sources (`aria-label`, `<label>`) and the shell building the tree through `Document::accessibility_tree` so a wrapper's override reaches it (`decision/a11y-tree-through-document-trait`). Matters: a virtual node with no DOM behind it is a new kind of tree node; whether and how it carries an author_id (`{owner}///{key}`) must be squared with this contract, and the commented `Widget::accessibility_tree` sits beside the trait path this entry fixed. Trap recorded there: the windowed stand ships no AccessKit adapter.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the founder's actionable-key rule: every element an agent can act on reads an author key, checked by `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`, role taken from the tree with no second mapping. Matters: the virtual node's author key is the same idea one level down; its trap — never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or role — and the rule that keys are authored, not derived, bind the declaration's key rules.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — made the snapshot consume the accessibility tree's role, name and focus with no second role or name mapping. Matters: the root of `decision/snapshot-model-single-source` and `decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model`; a closed role set declared on a virtual node must map onto the tree's roles, not become a parallel role/name mapping when «Virtual nodes as elements» later brings the nodes into the tree and snapshot.

**2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema** — recorded that the driver's schema defines no role or name set of its own; `role` and `name` are field names of its result nodes (row `decision/driver-schema-has-no-role-set`). Matters: the chunk's «role: a closed set» must not land as a driver-side role set; the fork on where the declaration lives (engine `Widget` vs Dioxus renderer) should keep the role set on the engine/tree side.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — made the tree refresh on change and defined what the engine's changed set marks (mutation, focus/checked, text input; not creation, hover, active, scroll, layout); the diff became a reader of the snapshot model. Matters: the «list at each paint vs callbacks with invalidation» fork decides whether a changed declaration marks the changed set; per `decision/changed-set-marks`, a paint alone marks nothing today, so a paint-time list would never refresh the tree unless the set is marked.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — the founder ratified the refresh on change and the changed-set contract (were PROVISIONAL). Matters: these are ratified contracts (`decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change`, `decision/changed-set-marks`, «one item»); any widening of what marks the set for virtual-node declarations is a change to a ratified row, a founder fork.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom, so both seven_guis binaries compile the tree override, snapshot and diff, neither builds a platform adapter. Matters: background for `decision/accessibility-feature-default-on` / `decision/agent-readers-behind-accessibility` and `absence/assistive-technology-reach` — a virtual-node reader or tree hook placed behind `accessibility` (or `custom-widget`) reaches the stand through this edge; no AT reads it.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — MCP tool results became a reader of the snapshot model, on the crossing the founder ratified 2026-10-10. Matters: the names' crossing fork rests on the same 2026-10-10 rule (authored text on a ratified carrier is a widening); this entry is the precedent for how a snapshot-model reader's crossing was ratified.

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** (the enabled-state walks, the list named) — retired the unnamed-list gap: every interactive-role node of the four lean tasks is named over nine roles, and the `&dyn Document` tree equals the document's, carrying stable ids only. Matters: origin of `decision/interactive-nodes-named` (guard `stand_accessibility_ids`); the scope's «name: non-empty» rule is the same invariant, and a virtual node with an interactive role must not break it once it enters the tree.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** — `unkeyed_actionable` reads 0 on Circle Drawer too; the click-without-role count pins Circle Drawer at 1. Matters: Circle Drawer's canvas is the first virtual-node host («Circle Drawer's circles as virtual nodes» is a later entry); its pinned counts are the baseline this chunk must leave unmoved.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** (§2–§4, §7: the toggle per role) — mapped `role="switch"` to `Switch` and read `aria-checked` on the five checkable roles alone (ratified 2026-10-18). Matters: the provenance of `contract/aria-role-mapping/role-switch`; a closed role set for virtual nodes that includes checkable roles meets this per-role state read.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the tree's focus falls back to the window) — `build_accessibility_tree` writes `focus` only where the focused node is among the built nodes, else the window, so the tree never names a node it did not build. Matters: a trap for nodes with no DOM behind them — virtual nodes are not engine nodes, so tree focus on one needs a deliberate rule (owned by the keyboard-path entry), not this fallback by accident.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (what the snapshot and an assistive technology read of an open list; how an open list's labels leave) — a row's own `bounds` read as a closed set inside the ratified crossing by the 2026-10-10 field rule; no `expanded` node key as the operator's call; option and group labels leaving only as pixels and the snapshot's `name`, ratified as a widening. Matters: the nearest precedent for engine-made nodes without their own DOM box (rows with their own bounds) and for authored text crossing as a widening — the shape the names' crossing fork and the region rule will be judged against.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the read-only UI graph reader; the clickable field) — `DioxusDocument::graph` holds one node per snapshot node, names and closed words only; `stand_graph` asserts no served id holds the reserved separator `///` (the `{owner}///{key}` form spelled by `virtual_node_id`, which the walk never calls); `NodeState.clickable` added. Matters: origin of `contract/node-id/reserved-separator` and `decision/ui-graph-one-node-per-snapshot-node` / `decision/ui-graph-carries-no-values`; this chunk is the first to produce `virtual_node_id` ids, so the «no served id holds ///» guard must stay true while nothing serves them, and the graph's reach is owned by «Virtual nodes in every read».

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (graph state registration and the bridge dispatch's write record) — apps register state through `use_graph_state` with authored `DeclaredWrite` declarations, an element's stable id or a `*`-ended prefix. Matters: precedent for an authored declaration API in dioxus-native-dom keyed on stable ids — relevant to the fork of where the virtual-node declaration lives (engine `Widget` vs Dioxus renderer).

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — one actionable rule `Readings` (focusable, interactive role, or current listeners) read by `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes`; `ActionableNode.keyed` true where the id holds no `/`; the `actions` verb writes ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only; `ACTIONABLE_AT_BOOT` pins Circle Drawer's tasks' counts. Matters: the scope's «author key holding no `/`» mirrors `keyed`'s reading, `owner` is the precedent for `{owner}` in the reserved form, and `contract/actions-answer/fields` plus the boot counts must stay unmoved since this chunk adds no carrier.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** (handler_coverage, a further reader of the UI graph) — `escher_driver::handler_coverage` reads the graph and answers ids, owner ids, event names and two counts only, no role or name. Matters: origin of `contract/handler-coverage/answer`, a row this chunk's declared names must not reach (its reach is «Virtual nodes in every read»).

**2026-11-13T07-43-19-wrap** — `decision/keyed-wire-form` ratified (the actions answer's `keyed` field). Matters: the `keyed` reading (id holds no `/`) is a standing wire form, so a virtual node's id `{owner}///{key}` reads unkeyed by today's rule — a conflict the later reads entry inherits and this chunk's id form should foresee.

**2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration** (2. A11y Strategy) — `~ decision/changed-set-marks`: a scroll that closes a list marks its select. Matters: one link in the changed-set row's chain of widenings; each mark added so far was an operator/founder ruling, the precedent for any mark a callback-with-invalidation declaration would need.

A11y Strategy) — `~ decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change` and `~ decision/accessibility-tree-through-document-method`: the tree is pushed again in a redraw after style resolve only when the changed set is non-empty, then cleared; a poll pushes no tree. **2026-11-21-engine-debts** (2. A11y Strategy) — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` to its current text (post-layout focus loss marks too; «layout alone do not»). Matters: the row as the picked rows hold it; a declaration-driven mark must be added to this ratified list by ruling, not silently.

**2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas** — `+ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only`: Circle Drawer's drawing area is one canvas node read by role and name alone, its circles reaching no DOM, snapshot, tree or UI graph. Matters: the row virtual nodes will eventually amend; this chunk declares nodes in process only, so the row's «reach no … accessibility tree or UI graph» must still hold at its wrap.

**2026-11-24T06-11-11-wrap** — `decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only` ratified by the founder, state standing. Matters: a ratified row; changing what leaves the canvas is a founder fork, consistent with the scope sending the names' crossing to P4.

**2026-11-24-upstream-sync-ahead-of-inside-the-canvas** — `+ absence/keyboard-drag-and-drop`: drag and drop is pointer-only with no keyboard or AT route. Matters: an absence in the picked rows' scope area, and the drag-and-drop security gap is carried freight on this chunk's wrap.

**2026-11-24-canvas-draw-commands** — `~ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only` (labels leave as canvas-verb draw commands, no text), `~ decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model` and `~ decision/snapshot-model-single-source` (the canvas read is no reader of the snapshot model). Matters: the latest canvas readers; a declared-node reader is a new in-process read that must say whether it is a snapshot-model reader, and «no label's text» is the bar the names' crossing fork meets.

**2026-11-24-canvas-lint** — `~ decision/circle-drawer-canvas-pixels-only` to its current text (labels reach the lint as truncated boxes, no text); PROVISIONAL on the escher overseer's delegate confirm, the founder away. Matters: the row stands provisional at this chunk's base; any edit to it here stacks on an unratified operation.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — the windowed AT witness owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (an active assistive technology this version does not reach); `docs/capabilities.md` publishes the accessibility reach by hand. Matters: background of `absence/assistive-technology-reach` — what an AT reads of virtual nodes stays unmeasured, and a new reach is written into `docs/capabilities.md` by hand.

Lets an app declare virtual nodes inside a canvas widget (an element the app paints from Rust through the custom widget): each node an author key, a role from a closed set, a non-empty name and a region inside the canvas's content box.
A declaration breaking a rule is not taken and nothing panics; each taken node gets the reserved id form owner, the /// separator, then the key; two nodes of one canvas with one key are refused.
The declared nodes are readable in process, validated and with their ids; no accessibility tree node, snapshot, diff, click, UI graph, actions or keyboard reach is added here.
The declaration's form, the names' crossing onto a carrier, the role set, where the declaration lives and the region's frame are founder's forks written to evidence, with the phase stopping at P4 with no default taken.
Two carried items ride the wrap: the security summary's drag-and-drop gaps and the test plan's one-host screenshot clause; neither adds a code step.

body: The served node id's reserved separator /// and the virtual node id form owner///key: a taken node's id is spelled through it, and a key holding / is refused so the id stays one node's.

A declared node's role drawn from a closed set; its relation to the existing role mapping (role attribute, element, else Unknown) and to the driver schema defining no role or name set is a fork the plan writes, not a choice it takes.
A declared node's name is non-empty and is author-written text; interactive nodes carry a name.

The names' crossing: author text on a ratified carrier is a widening, so a declared name or key reaches no snapshot, MCP result, UI graph or log field in this chunk; whether it ever does is the founder's fork.

A declaration breaking a rule (empty key, key with /, role outside the set, empty name, region outside the content box, duplicate key in one canvas) is not taken, stands for no node, and panics on no path.
The region is held in the canvas's content-box frame, the frame the custom widget paints in and hears pointer events in.
The in-process read of what a canvas declares now, validated and with ids, adds no driver verb, cause, carrier, log field or span and no reading on the socket, command line, MCP or a kept check.
The accessibility tree built through the document's own method and its refresh on change stay untouched: virtual nodes enter no AccessKit tree here, that belongs to the later entry.
Circle Drawer's drawing area stays one named canvas node with pixels only; its circles as virtual nodes belong to a later entry.
Accessibility assertions are Rust tests: each new test of a declaration's rules and refusals is such a test, a control entering the plan with its red reading.
The test plan's no-screenshot-step row and its one-host clause, carried to this chunk's wrap report, against canvas-only shot digests held equal across three hosts.
The drag-and-drop gaps (OS drag-and-drop as untrusted input with no keyboard route, the dropped-file reader with no path restriction) carried to this chunk's wrap leaf pass, never written by hand.

body: Keyboard navigation rows (Tab order, focus fixup, activation keys, range inputs, select lists, Cells grid, CRUD list): the canvas keyboard path is a later entry.
Visual design verification rows (contrast thresholds, lint contrast findings, scrollbar thumbs, select list colours, scheme and zoom): the chunk paints nothing new and adds no lint finding.

ARIA property and state reads (aria-checked, aria-pressed, aria-expanded, aria-labelledby and the rest) and hidden or inert content rules: virtual nodes carry no ARIA attributes and enter no tree here.
Snapshot field contracts (checked, enabled, value, password value, select rows and bounds, file input value) and snapshot text tokens: a virtual node reaches no snapshot in this chunk.
Driver click refusals, actions answer causes and handler coverage: click and the covered, off-screen, disabled and stale refusals belong to later entries.
Select and optgroup behaviour, form event values and UI graph state registration: no form control or graph state changes.
Platform adapter rows (accesskit_xplat, no adapter on the stand, adapter creation order, adapter tree equals harness tree): no adapter changes.
Cognitive accessibility rows (invalid state stated beyond colour or class): no invalid state is touched.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the reserved virtual-node id form) — added the fifth, reserved id form `{owner}///{key}` that no tier produces and no walk writes, spelled by the public `VIRTUAL_KEY_SEPARATOR` and `virtual_node_id`, which answers `None` for an empty or `/`-bearing key. This is the founder's P4 fork 2 answer, and `stand_graph` measured no served id holding `///`. It is exactly what this chunk first fills: contract/dioxus-bridge/virtual-node-id and contract/stable-element-id/virtual-node-id. The key rules (non-empty, no `/`) are already the function's own. A taken node must keep "no served tier id holds `///`" true.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the UI graph crosses the ratified carriers; `clickable`; the graph reader) — `graph` and `clickable` crossed as a ratified widening on the founder's own forks, with the graph's nodes defined as snapshot nodes. This is the precedent for a new reading over the screen's nodes: every graph node is a snapshot node, and `clickable` is a closed bool inside a ratified carrier. Planning should know that nodes with no DOM behind them would reach graph, actions and coverage. Those consumers belong to «Virtual nodes in every read», not this chunk.

**2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** — registered `element_id` and `element_ids` and the id grammar: computed on demand, written to neither the DOM nor the vdom, and with no `NodeId`, `ElementId`, `ScopeId` or pointer in an id. The owner part of `{owner}///{key}` is the canvas element's id under this grammar. That makes contract/stable-element-id/no-process-local-values and element-id binding on what a virtual node's id may hold.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the anchored tier `{key}//{segment}` (one-component reach, ratified by the founder) and `unkeyed_actionable`. It set the tier-distinctness rule that only an anchored path holds `//`, which the later `///` form had to stay distinct from. It also left a trap: `UnkeyedActionable.node` is a process-local `NodeId`, so no wire form may carry it. The same applies to any in-process virtual-node record this chunk adds.

**2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep** (every stand task keyed) — Circle Drawer's canvas reads the author id `circle-canvas`, and `unkeyed_actionable()` returns nothing on every stand task. A canvas owner keyed by author key is the owner half of `{owner}///{key}` on the stand. A keyed owner keeps the virtual id stable under the anchored rules.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — added the defaulted `Document::accessibility_tree()`, which `DioxusDocument` overrides to set `author_id` to the stable id, and which the shell calls for the platform tree. contract/document-trait/accessibility-tree is the extension seam later virtual-node entries will use. Its noted trap: a feature-gated item can pass under `--workspace` and be compiled out under `-p blitz-tests`.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — the snapshot node is every element the accessibility tree keeps, and the standing rule is that the snapshot derives no role or name of its own. Today's snapshot model is element-only. The role set and name this chunk declares must not become a second source that disagrees with the tree once «Virtual nodes as elements» lands.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** (the adapter's third class) — the builder's state reads widened the platform-adapter crossing by a new author-derived class. This was ratified with the rule that a later attribute read keeps that shape: a closed set, no text carried out. This is the precedent for a closed role set. A declared non-empty name is free author text, so a closed set does not cover it.

**2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts** (descriptions on the adapter crossing) — a fourth content class, descriptions (free page text), goes to the platform adapter only, ratified as upstream's behaviour, and the snapshot reads no description. This underlies decision/adapter-crossing-carries-descriptions: authored free text has reached the adapter and not the driver's carriers. It is a lead for the names'-crossing fork.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — registered the session socket, ratified by the founder, with the standing rule that the first request carrying an id, a name, a value, snapshot text or a diff is a new crossing question. This is the root of decision/new-carrier-widens-boundary and of the names'-crossing fork this chunk must put to the founder.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** (the session socket carries a call and its answer) — the second widening: ids, accessible names and masked values leave by design, ratified by the founder. «The next surface that carries them asks again.» This is the basis of decision/socket-carries-driver-calls and decision/session-over-unix-socket. A virtual node's name riding an existing answer is the question this entry says must be asked again.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — the MCP role's stdio crossing was ratified with no listener (decision/mcp-stdio-crossing), with the standing rule that the next surface carrying a call or a screen's content is a new crossing question. If names cross, MCP is one of the carriers the fork must measure.

**2026-10-12-self-description** (fixed program text on the ratified carriers) — the program's own fixed `'static` table text rides the ratified carriers, while text from a page, a call or a screen still widens. This is decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers. A declared virtual-node name is app-authored text, not program text, so it falls on the widening side.

**2026-11-16-error-text-in-the-answer** — `caused` began carrying an app's own authored messages and fields across every carrier, ratified on the founder's word. decision/no-node-id-across-session's list gained "a step's caused text". This is the nearest precedent for app-authored text crossing a ratified carrier as an explicit widening. It is a measured-cost lead for the names'-crossing fork.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the list on the carriers, a boundary widening) — a select list's painted labels crossing as pixels in a shot was named a boundary widening and ratified by the founder. A row's `bounds` stayed inside the ratified crossing, and no `expanded` node key was added. This is the precedent for content with no DOM box of its own reaching the carriers, and for keeping that content off the node keys.

**2026-11-23-canvas-in-a-headless-shot** — added decision/canvas-crosses-as-pixels, ratified for all carriers, and decision/harness-paints-custom-widgets (the harness turns on blitz-paint's `custom-widget`). This was the first statement of how a canvas's content crosses, and the base the later draw-command crossing replaced.

**2026-11-23-canvas-placement-and-text** — added decision/custom-widget-content-box-paint, later restated as ratified: the widget paints at its content box times the scale, at the content origin inside the element's transform, unclipped. It also added `Widget::fonts` and `BaseDocument::font_ctx`. The scope holds a virtual node's region in the content-box frame on the strength of this decision. Its region rule must use the same box (border and padding off, floored at 0).

**2026-11-23-circle-drawer-on-a-canvas** — added decision/widget-click-point-content-box (a click point is read against the content box, measured off by border and padding when read against the client rect) and decision/widget-click-synthesis. It also added Circle Drawer's in-process-only boot, served by no role, and decision/canvas-placement-at-click-centre, which was provisional and later ratified. The pointer frame the scope cites for the region is this one. The stand's Circle Drawer is the canvas a later entry turns into virtual nodes.

**2026-11-23-canvas-shot-across-hosts** — added a canvas-only shot held byte-equal on three CI hosts as an exception to decision/no-screenshot-in-cross-os-byte-check, and restated committed-stand-checks' reason. This explains the test-plan CARRY cry-ax6q6t4w (the one-host clause) that this chunk's wrap must carry.

**2026-11-24-canvas-draw-commands** (canvas crossing) — retired canvas-crosses-as-pixels for decision/canvas-crossing: draw commands cross every carrier as the `canvas` verb's answer, ratified. It added "canvas readings" to decision/no-node-id-across-session and decision/canvas-reading-diffable, plus provisional decision/canvas-dump-in-parts. These are the standing crossing rows a virtual node's id, role and name would extend. The draw-commands-grouped-by-node work belongs to the Circle Drawer entry.

**2026-11-24-canvas-draw-commands** (the canvas verb and `custom_widget_scene`) — added contract/paint/custom-widget-scene: one widget's scene outside a raster, behind `custom-widget`, flagged upstreamable. It also added the harness's `canvas_scene`, `Session::canvas`, the canvas target-check arm and the verb table at sixteen. This is the in-process read path and the widget-scene seam beside which a declaration read would sit.

**2026-11-24-canvas-lint** — added decision/canvas-label-region (provisional): a label's region is the widget's content box cut by each pushed clip, layer or mask path's bounding box, mapped through its transform, and by the element's clip region. It also added absence/canvas-lint-checks-beyond-truncation and decision/skrifa-glyph-outline-bounds (provisional). This is the nearest existing in-canvas region rule. A virtual node's region "inside the canvas's content box" must be stated consistently with it.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** (the coverage reader and its limits) — states "handlers inside a canvas not counted, deferred to 0.4.0" as a limit with its owner. Virtual nodes are this version's path to that deferred limit. The scope assigns coverage to «Virtual nodes in every read», so this chunk must not claim the limit's discharge.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the one actionable rule; `actions`) — added `actionable_nodes`, the one actionable rule, `ActionableNode { id, owner, keyed }`, and `keyed` as the actionable-key check's first wire form (decision/keyed-wire-form, decision/actionable-elements-keyed). `keyed` reads true where the id holds no `/`. **2026-11-13T07-43-19-wrap** — decision/keyed-wire-form and decision/actions-keyed-reading went from provisional to standing on the founder's word. The keyed reading's `/` test is now a ratified wire form, so the virtual form's interaction with it is not loose.

A declaration made at render or paint time must respect this ordering, and the merge surface is owned by the upstream-sync CARRY.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — added the changed set (has_changes / take_changed_nodes, node creation marking nothing, drained ids read through `get_node`) and the diff kept apart from the changed set. **2026-11-19-upstream-sync-ahead-of-the-debts** (the platform tree refresh moved to redraw) — changed decision/accessibility-tree-refresh-on-change and contract/accessibility-tree/platform-refresh: on a redraw, after resolve, the shell hands the adapter a fresh tree when the changed set is non-empty, and a poll refreshes nothing. body: The Widget trait of blitz-dom's custom widget: a canvas element whose content the app paints from Rust is where virtual nodes are declared; whether the declaration lives on the engine Widget trait or in the Dioxus renderer is a fork.
The author key of a virtual node: non-empty and holding no slash, so that it reads as an author key in the stable element id tiers.

The reserved virtual node id form: owner stable id, the virtual key separator, then the key, produced only through the virtual node id function of the stable element ids and the Dioxus bridge; nothing produces such a node before this chunk.
A virtual node id holds no process-local value and no NodeId: its owner part is the canvas element's stable id, and tier distinctness between the virtual form and the other id tiers holds.
The virtual node role: a closed set of roles; the set itself is a fork written with the others.

The virtual node name: non-empty, and it is text the app author wrote; authored text on a ratified carrier is a widening of the session boundary, so whether a name or key crosses any carrier is the names' crossing fork.

The virtual node region: inside the canvas's content box and held in the content-box frame, the frame the custom widget paints in and hears pointer events in; the region's frame and its rule are a fork.

Validation of a declaration is on untrusted input: a declaration breaking any rule is not taken, no node stands for it, and no code path panics; any expect or unwrap on that path needs its justification.
Duplicate keys within one canvas are refused so that one id names one node.

body: The virtual node declaration on a canvas widget: author key, role, name and region, and the rules each must meet (key non-empty with no slash, role from a closed set, name non-empty, region inside the canvas's content box).
Refusal of a broken declaration: no node stands for it and no panic path is reached on untrusted input — the no-panic security rule binds the validation code and each refused case owes its own test.

The reserved owner-key id form of a virtual node and the element-id virtual form contract: each taken node's id is the canvas element's stable id, the separator, then the key, built through the existing virtual id function and never spelled by hand.
Duplicate keys within one canvas refused, so one id names one node only.
The region held in the canvas's content-box frame, the frame the custom widget paints in and hears pointer events in; a region outside it is refused.
The in-process read of what a canvas declares now, validated and with its ids — the only new reading this chunk adds.

Nothing crosses a carrier: no driver verb, argument kind, refusal cause, session error, exit status, carrier, log field or span is added, and no declared name or key reaches a log line, stderr line, recording or answer — names and ids stay out of stand and driver logs, which hold fixed words and counts only.
